Reject requests, refuse or decline to allow access to international actors such
as observers, humanitarian agencies, and peacekeeping forces.

1246.name: Refuse to de-escalate military engagement
1246.description:
Reject requests, refuse, or decline to stop ghting or take measures to ease
military conict or tension.

125.name: Reject proposal to meet, discuss, negotiate
125.description: Refuse to meet, discuss, or negotiate.

126.name: Reject mediation
126.description: Refuse involvement of mediators or mediation initiatives.

127.name: Reject plan, agreement to settle dispute
127.description:
Reject a proposal or request for a nal, comprehensive settlement, peace
proposal, or resolution.

128.name: Defy norms, law
128.description: Disobey, challenge, or resist laws or norms.

129.name: Veto
129.description:
Refuse to assent or formally reject legislative proposal, recommendation, or
resolution.
Example
The United States on Wednesday vetoed a Security Council resolution cen-
suring as a violation of international law its military sweep of the Nicaraguan
ambassadors home in Panama on December 29.
2.13
THREATEN

130.name: Threaten, not specied below
130.description:
All threats, coercive or forceful warnings with serious potential repercussions,
not otherwise specied.

131.name: Threaten non-force, not specied below
131.description: All non-force threats not otherwise specied.

1311.name: Threaten to reduce or stop aid
1311.description: Threaten to reduce or stop providing material aid.

1312.name: Threaten to boycott, embargo, or sanction
1312.description:
Threaten to restrict normal economic interactions by imposing sanctions,
boycotts, or embargoes.

1313.name: Threaten to reduce or break relations
1313.description: Threaten to reduce or formally sever ties.

132.name: Threaten with administrative sanctions, not specied below
132.description:
Threaten to impose or expand non-force administrative restrictions and
penalties not otherwise specied.

1321.name: Threaten with restrictions on political freedoms
1321.description:
Threaten to impose or expand restrictions on fundamental freedoms, such
as freedoms of speech, expression, and assembly.

1322.name: Threaten to ban political parties or politicians
1322.description: Threaten to ban political activities of particular parties or individuals.

1323.name: Threaten to impose curfew
1323.description:
Threaten to enforce a deadline beyond which inhabitants of an area are not
permitted to be on the streets or in public places.
Example
President Laurent Gbagbo announced on Sunday that he will extend the
night-time curfew in Algiers in response to recent unrest within the city.
Example Note
Note that the future tense used in the lead implies a threat.
Example
President Abdelaziz Bouteicka threatened to institute a curfew in Algiers
in response to recent unrest within the city.

1324.name: Threaten to impose state of emergency or martial law
1324.description:
Threaten with suspending certain given rights or the whole constitution by
imposing state of emergency or military rule.
Example
Iraqs interim government announced that it is prepared to impose mar-
tial law as street battles raged in central Baghdad between insurgents and
security forces.

133.name: Threaten political dissent
133.description:
Threaten to mobilize or engage in actions of political dissent such as protest
demonstrations, hunger strikes, strikes or boycotts, physical obstructions
into buildings or areas, and riots.
Example
Radical French farmers said on Friday they would blockade Paris from Mon-
day night to demand an end to the European Communitys drastic farm
reform.
Example
Druze inhabitants of the Syrian Golan Heights threatened today to hold a
general strike unless Israel rescinded its annexation of the region within 10
days.

134.name: Threaten to halt negotiations
134.description: Threaten to break-up or withdraw from discussion, negotiation, or meeting.

136.name: Threaten to halt international involvement (non-mediation)
136.description:
Threaten to reduce or stop international intervention by expelling or with-
drawing observers, humanitarian agencies, peacekeepers, etc.

138.name: Threaten with military force, not specied below
138.description: Threaten to use force not otherwise specied.

1381.name: Threaten blockade
1381.description:
Threaten to prevent entry into and/or exit from a territory using military
measures.

1382.name: Threaten occupation
1382.description: Threaten to occupy, seize control of the whole or part of a territory.

1383.name: Threaten unconventional attack
1383.description: Threaten to use unconventional violence, including terrorist activities.

1384.name: Threaten conventional attack
1384.description: Threaten to attack, use conventional weapons against a party.

1385.name: Threaten unconventional mass violence
1385.description:
Threaten to use force potentially aecting large masses of people, includ-
ing the use of weapons of mass destruction (nuclear or chemical-biological-
radiological attacks), mass expulsions or killings, as well as ethnic cleansing.

139.name: Give ultimatum
139.description: Give a nal warning, ultimate demand or order.

140.name: Engage in political dissent, not specied below.
140.description:
All civilian demonstrations and other collective actions carried out as
protests against the target actor not otherwise specied.

141.name: Demonstrate or rally, not specied below
141.description:
Dissent collectively, publicly show negative feelings or opinions; rally, gather
to protest a policy, action, or actor(s).

1411.name: Demonstrate or rally for leadership change
1411.description: Dissent collectively, gather, or rally demanding leadership change.

1412.name: Demonstrate or rally for policy change
1412.description: Dissent collectively, gather, or rally demanding policy change.

1413.name: Demonstrate for rights
1413.description:
Dissent collectively, gather, or rally demanding political, social, economic,
or other rights.

1414.name: Demonstrate for change in institutions, regime
1414.description:
Dissent collectively, gather, or rally demanding major institutional, consti-
tutional, or regime change.

142.name: Conduct hunger strike, not specied below
142.description:
Protest by refusing to eat until certain demands are met, not further speci-
ed.

1421.name: Conduct hunger strike for leadership change
1421.description: Refuse to eat until demands for leadership change are met.

1422.name: Conduct hunger strike for policy change
1422.description: Refuse to eat until demands for policy reform are met.

1423.name: Conduct hunger strike for rights
1423.description:
Refuse to eat until demands for political, social, economic, or other rights
are met.

1424.name: Conduct hunger strike for change in institutions, regime
1424.description:
Refuse to eat until demands for major institutional, constitutional, or regime
change.

143.name: Conduct strike or boycott, not specied below
143.description:
Protest by refusing to work or cooperate until certain demands are met, not
specied further.

1431.name: Conduct strike or boycott for leadership change
1431.description: Refuse to work or cooperate until demands for leadership change are met.

1432.name: Conduct strike or boycott for policy change
1432.description: Refuse to work or cooperate until demands for policy reform are met.

1433.name: Conduct strike or boycott for rights
1433.description:
Refuse to work or cooperate until demands for political, social, economic, or
other rights are met.

1434.name: Conduct strike or boycott for change in institutions, regime
1434.description:
Refuse to work or cooperate until demands for major institutional, consti-
tutional, or regime change.

144.name: Obstruct passage, block, not specied below
144.description:
Protest by blocking entry and/or exit into building or area, not otherwise
specied.

1441.name: Obstruct passage to demand leadership change
1441.description: Obstruct passage, block entry/exit to demand leadership change.

1442.name: Obstruct passage to demand policy change
1442.description: Obstruct passage, block entry/exit to demand policy reform.

1443.name: Obstruct passage to demand rights
1443.description:
Obstruct passage, block entry/exit to demand political, social, economic, or
other rights.

1444.name: Obstruct passage to demand change in institutions, regime
1444.description:
Obstruct passage, block entry/exit to demand major institutional, constitu-
tional, or regime change.

145.name: Protest violently, riot, not specied below
145.description: Protest forcefully, in a potentially destructive manner, not further specied.

1451.name: Engage in violent protest for leadership change
1451.description:
Protest forcefully, in a potentially destructive manner, to demand leadership
change.

1452.name: Engage in violent protest to demand policy change
1452.description:
Protest forcefully, in a potentially destructive manner, to demand policy
reform.

1453.name: Engage in violent protest to demand rights
1453.description:
Protest forcefully, in a potentially destructive manner, to demand political,
social, economic, or other rights.

1454.name: Engage in violent protest to demand change in institutions, regime
1454.description:
Protest forcefully, in a potentially destructive manner, to demand major
institutional, constitutional, or regime change.

150.name: Exhibit military or police power, not specied below
150.description:
All military or police moves that fall short of the actual use of force, not
otherwise specied.

152.name: Increase military alert status
152.description: Heighten military readiness and caution; be prepared to use force.

153.name: Mobilize or increase police power
153.description: Increase the number of military personnel and/or weapons.

154.name: Mobilize or increase armed forces
154.description: Increase the number of military personnel and/or weapons.

155.name: Mobilize or increase cyber-forces
155.description: Increase the capacity to wage cyber-warfare.

160.name: Reduce relations, not specied below
160.description:
All reductions in normal, routine, or cooperative relations not otherwise
specied.

161.name: Reduce or break diplomatic relations
161.description: Curtail, decrease, break, or terminate diplomatic exchange.

162.name: Reduce or stop material aid, not specied below
162.description: Reductions or terminations of aid not otherwise specied.

1621.name: Reduce or stop economic assistance
1621.description:
Decrease or terminate provision of economic aid.
Example
Japan said on Tuesday it had halted economic aid to Yugoslavia in line with
Western eorts to end the ghting there.

1622.name: Reduce or stop military assistance
1622.description:
Decrease or terminate provision of military aid.
Example
The United States suspended part of a military aid program for Bosnia aimed
at bringing Bosnian Croat and Moslem armed forces together as a unied
identity, the New York Times reported on Friday.

1623.name: Reduce or stop humanitarian assistance
1623.description:
Decrease or terminate provision of humanitarian aid.
Example
The United Nations on Tuesday reduced food supplies to the biggest Cam-
bodian refugee camp in Thailand because rice was being diverted to outside
users, relief ocials said.

163.name: Impose embargo, boycott, or sanctions
163.description:
Stop or restrict commercial or other material exchange as a form of protest
or punishment.
Example
President Bill Clinton has imposed sanctions on the Taliban religious faction
that controls Afghanistan for its support of suspected terrorist Osama bin
Laden, the White House said Tuesday.

166.name: Expel or withdraw, not specied below
166.description: Terminate the presence of groups or organizations not otherwise specied.

1661.name: Expel or withdraw peacekeepers
1661.description: Terminate the deployment or presence of peacekeeping forces.

1662.name: Expel or withdraw inspectors, observers
1662.description: Terminate the presence of inspectors or other observers.

1663.name: Expel or withdraw aid agencies
1663.description:
Terminate the presence of aid agencies or other non-governmental organiza-
tions helping civilians.

170.name: Coerce, not specied below
170.description:
Repression, violence against civilians, or their rights or properties not oth-
erwise specied.
Example
Turkish
police
prevented
the
demonstration
staged
by
students
at
Cumhuriyet University near AKP oces in Sivas on 15 October to protest
the decision of sending troops to Iraq.

171.name: Seize or damage property, not specied below
171.description:
Use of force against property or violation of property rights not otherwise
specied.

1711.name: Conscate property
1711.description: Use force to take control of somebody elses property, conscate, expropriate.

1712.name: Destroy property
1712.description:
Use force to destroy, demolish property.
Example
Afghan guerillas blew up three main electric power lines leading into Kabul
last month and nearly one third of the citys power supply is still down, the
Czechoslovak news agency Ceteka reported from Kabul today.
Example
Jewish settlers in the West Bank city of Hebron set re to the oces of
the Palestinian administrators of Muslim property overnight following the
killing of an Israeli man, Palestinian residents said Sunday.
Example
Israeli army bulldozers demolished Palestinian homes and civilian buildings
in southern Gaza on Sunday, Palestinian ocials and US witnesses said.

172.name: Impose administrative sanctions, not specied below
172.description:
Formal decrees, laws, or policies aimed at curbing the rights of civilians not
otherwise specied.

1721.name: Impose restrictions on political freedoms
1721.description:
Violate or impose limitations on fundamental political rights such as free-
doms of speech, expression, and assembly.

1722.name: Ban political parties or politicians
1722.description:
Prevent establishment or activities of political parties or politicians.
Example
President Yoweri Museveni has banned Ugandan opposition candidates from
participating in the upcoming elections.

1723.name: Impose curfew
1723.description:
Set a deadline beyond which inhabitants of an area are not permitted to be
on the streets or in public places.
Example
Turkish authorities have imposed a curfew in the town of Cizre in southeast-
ern Turkey after a demonstration over fraud allegations in Sundays local
elections, security sources said here Tuesday.

1724.name: Impose state of emergency or martial law
1724.description:
Suspend normal constitutional rights and provisions by installing state of
emergency or military rule.
Example
The military government of President Prosper Avril declared a 30-day state
of siege in Haiti on Saturday, suspending parts of the constitution and ar-
resting political opponents, a spokeswoman for the U.S. embassy said.

173.name: Arrest, detain
173.description: Legal or extrajudicial arrests, detentions, or imprisonments.

174.name: Expel or deport individuals
174.description:
Formal removal or expulsion of individuals from territories, typically follow-
ing legal proceedings.

175.name: Use repression
175.description:
Actively repress collective actions of dissent by forcing subjugation through
crowd control tactics, arrests, etc.

176.name: Attack cybernetically
176.description: Illegal or unauthorized attack on computers, networks, or accounts.

180.name: Use unconventional violence, not specied below
180.description:
Use of unconventional forms of violence which do not require high levels of
organization or conventional weaponry, not otherwise specied.

181.name: Abduct, hijack, take hostage
181.description:
Kidnap, take hostage, hijack, or forcibly seize control of an aircraft, car, bus,
ship, etc.
Example
Afghan rebels have kidnapped up to 16 Soviet civilian advisers from a town
bazaar and exploded a series of bombs in the capital Kabul, western diplo-
matic sources in neighboring Pakistan said today.

182.name: Physically assault, not specied below
182.description:
Attack physical well-being of individuals without the use of weaponry, not
otherwise specied.

1821.name: Sexually assault
1821.description: Sexually abuse, assault sexual integrity of individuals.

1822.name: Torture
1822.description: Torture, inict extreme pain on individuals.

1823.name: Kill by physical assault
1823.description:
Kill individuals by physically assaulting them without the use of weaponry,
through beating, torture, lynching, etc.

183.name:
Conduct suicide, car, or other non-military bombing, not specied
below
183.description:
The use of explosive devices or improvised explosives outside of military
engagements.

1831.name: Carry out suicide bombing
1831.description:
Carry out bomb attack with the intention of causing own death as well as
other casualties.

1832.name: Carry out vehicular bombing
1832.description: Blow up a car or other vehicle to cause damage to surroundings.

1833.name: Carry out roadside bombing
1833.description:
Detonate explosives on the roadside to cause damage and casualties to
passers-by.

1834.name: Carry out location bombing
1834.description:
The use of pre-placed explosive device(s) with the intent of causing casualties
and or/structural damage.

184.name: Use as human shield
184.description:
Use civilians as buer on the front lines or in other dangerous environments.
Example
The Sri Lankan army has been holding thousands of Tamil civilian refugees
as human shields in the battle zones of the southern sector of the Jana
peninsula, according to a press release by the Liberation Tigers.

185.name: Attempt to assassinate
185.description: Attempt but fail to kill politically signicant and inuential persons.

186.name: Assassinate
186.description: Kill politically signicant and inuential persons.

190.name: Use conventional military force, not specied below
190.description:
All uses of conventional force and acts of war typically by organized armed
groups not otherwise specied.

191.name: Impose blockade, restrict movement
191.description: Prevent entry into and/or exit from a territory using armed forces.

192.name: Occupy territory
192.description:
Occupy, seize control of a territory using armed forces.
Example
Vietnamese-led forces have retaken a strategic village in Western Kampuchea
after erce ghting with guerrillas who overran it late last month, Thai
military sources said today.
Example
Burmese troops have captured part of a Karen guerrilla stronghold on the
Thai border after ve days of ghting, Thai police here said on Monday.
Example
Israel today mounted its long-threatened invasion of South Lebanon, plough-
ing through the United Nations lines on the coast of south of Tyre and
thrusting forward in at least to inland areas.

193.name: Fight with small arms and light weapons
193.description:
Attack using small arms and light weapons such as ries, machine-guns, and
mortar shells.

194.name: Fight with artillery and tanks
194.description: Attack using artillery, tanks, and rocket re.

195.name: Employ aerial weapons, not specied below
195.description: Attack, bomb from air, not specied below.

1951.name: Employ precision-guided aerial munitions
1951.description:
The use of aerial weapons that utilize internal and/or remote sensing and
guidance controls to strike specic targets.

1952.name: Employ remotely piloted aerial munitions
1952.description:
The use of remotely piloted or unmanned aerial platforms for the delivery
or ordinance.

196.name: Violate ceasere
196.description: Reinitiate ghting in the midst of a formal or informal ceasere or truce.

200.name: Use massive unconventional force, not specied below
200.description:
All uses of unconventional force that are meant to cause mass destruction,
casualties, and suering not otherwise specied.

201.name: Engage in mass expulsion
201.description: Force large groups of people or populations out of some territory.

202.name: Engage in mass killings
202.description:
Kill a substantial number of people, typically with the intention of ridding
a territory of a particular group of people.

203.name: Engage in ethnic cleansing
203.description: Use mass expulsions and/or mass killings targeting a specic ethnic group.

204.name: Use weapons of mass destruction, not specied below
204.description:
Attack with unconventional weapons that are meant to cause massive de-
struction and casualties.

2041.name: Use chemical, biological, or radiological weapons
2041.description: Attack using chemical, biological, or radiological weapons.
